text:
maria: Heads-up — saw 3 OOMs in prod in the last hour that all correlate to long convo requests (context > 25k tokens). Started after the kernel-selector change rolled yesterday. Pattern looks like KV cache growth then eviction churn then hard OOM. Stack traces look like kv_alloc failing in slab_compact and then the runtime panics.

ryan: Can you paste the minimal log snippet and which model/slot this hit? I want to see sequence length and slab stats.

maria: Pasting minimal repro logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-17T10:02:34Z] req=abcd slot=gpu-2 model=redwood-3b sequence=27840 tokens
[2026-03-17T10:02:34Z] kv_cache: alloc(55239168) slab_used=432MB slab_free=24MB frag=0.78
[2026-03-17T10:02:35Z] kv_cache: evict start candidate=older_segments=120 keep_recent=4
[2026-03-17T10:02:35Z] slab_compact: scanned=180 items freed=0 heavy_frag
[2026-03-17T10:02:35Z] oom: kv_alloc failed wanted=55239168 avail=16777216
runtime: panic: OOM during kv_alloc
```

anita: That looks like fragmentation-heavy failure - compact scanning didn't free contiguous region. We saw similar when per-kernel allocations changed alignment after the new kernel-selector. Fragmentation + large contiguous alloc triggers OOM even if total free memory nominally > request.

kevin: Quick mitigation we can flip: enable kv-paging (disk spill) and reduce KV_CACHE_MAX_SLAB_BYTES for longconvo routes. Config suggestion to flip via runtime flags (hot):
```
RUNTIME_FLAGS=--kv_enable_paging=1 --kv_slack_threshold=0.15 --kv_max_slab_bytes=268435456
```
This will let large contexts spill to local NVMe rather than forcing contiguous GPU allocations.

maria: Do we have perf cost estimate for paging? We need SLO tradeoffs.

ryan: From perf tests, single-page spill adds ~30-120ms per affected request depending on overlap. For >25k contexts it avoids OOM 95% of the time; cost is mostly latency tail. We can gate by request size.

sre-oncall: Incident metrics: 3 OOMs, 12 failed requests, error-rate bump +0.07% across region us-east-1 between 09:58-10:08; no customer visible partial data loss but increased 5xx. Suggest circuit breaker: return 503 + Retry-After when mem pressure high, and publish alert when slab_free < 10% for >30s.

kevin: Agreed. Also propose a graceful-degrade path: when allocation fails, try incremental summarization fallback. Implementation sketch:
1) Detect kv_alloc OOM for request with sequence > threshold.
2) spawn summarizer that consumes head segments and produces condensed summary tokens (cost small).
3) replace earliest segments with summary and retry generation (expected to shrink KV footprint by ~x5).
Edge-case: summarizer itself must be stateless and capped.

anita: That approach is neat and avoids spilling for many cases. Needs safety: ensure summary is deterministic enough for model quality, run on CPU if GPU unavailable. Put a per-request budget.

maria: Can we do a fast mitigation now while we build summarizer? Something low-risk hotfix.

ryan: Hotfix plan: 1) revert kernel-selector roll to previous stable for canary hosts (rolling back the alignment/regression) 2) enable kv_enable_paging globally with conservative limits 3) add slab_free alert and circuit breaker 4) instrument a pprof-like memprofile to capture slab fragmentation snapshot on next OOM.

infra-bot: [alert] Deploy rollback triggered by @ryan to canary pool at 10:20Z (deploy-id: d-20260317-9876).

anita: I'll prototype the summarizer quick PoC tomorrow AM. Kevin can own paging config and SRE can own the circuit breaker.

kevin: I'll push a patch to flip KV flags behind feature flag and set rollout to 100% in 10m if no regressions. Also adding a safe default: if kv_enable_paging=1 but disk not available, we will 503 instead of attempting big alloc.

sre-oncall: I'll add the alert and a runbook step to toggle the feature flag and annotate when to rollback. Also schedule a postmortem if we see >3 OOMs in 24h.

maria: Thanks. Follow-ups: please post memprofile snapshot to this thread once available and set an owner for the summarizer PoC. I'll start a perf job: longconvo load replay (seq up to 40k) to validate paging latency.

ryan: Assigning owners: kevin -> paging config rollout, anita -> summarizer PoC, sre-oncall -> alerts/runbook, maria -> perf job + verification.

kevin: quick config snippet I will push to k8s configmap: 
```
kv:
  enable_paging: true
  max_slab_bytes: 268435456  # 256MB per slab
  slab_slack_ratio: 0.12
  disk_spill_path: /var/local/kvspill
  spill_io_budget_mbps: 200
```

anita: For PoC summarizer, idea is to run a small prompt that condenses ~5k tokens -> ~200-400 tokens. We'll keep it off by default and gate by the OOM detection path.

maria: Good. Let's keep this thread as the coordination point. Post memprofile + perf results here. Good work :rocket:

ryan: I'll monitor canary rollback and report back in 15m.

infra-bot: [deploy] rollback to stable completed at 10:32Z (deploy-id: d-20260317-9876, hosts: canary pool).
